key_insight: The paper learns phase-field models directly from ab initio-quality molecular dynamics by deriving the mesoscopic equation from Mori-Zwanzig projection and fitting the unknown free energy and mobility with neural networks.
engineering_relevance: This enables quantum-accurate microstructure evolution simulations at mesoscopic length and time scales, making it useful for predicting phase stability, segregation, and nucleation in materials under realistic conditions.
method: Derive a phase-field equation from molecular dynamics using Mori-Zwanzig projection onto species-density fields.
Parameterize the unknown nonlocal free energy and mobility with neural networks.
Train on short MD trajectories generated by machine-learning interatomic potentials of ab initio accuracy.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated on Fe-B and H-He systems, reproducing the FeB4 pressure-dependent stability shift and the helium-rain immiscibility/nucleation behavior in a 2.2-million-atom equivalent column simulation.
watch_item: Model reliability depends on the quality and coverage of the training trajectories, so extrapolation to unseen compositions or conditions may be uncertain.
